title: Temperature & Heat
summary: Temperature measures molecular kinetic energy; heat is energy that flows between objects at different temperatures. $Q=mc\Delta T$ warms things, $Q=mL$ changes phase, and materials expand as $\Delta L=\alpha L\Delta T$. Heat moves by conduction, convection, and radiation.

heat.plain: Energy transferred by a temperature difference.

specific heat.plain: Heat to warm 1 kg by 1 K.

concept_sections.heading: Temperature vs heat
concept_sections.explanation: Temperature is a measure of molecular kinetic energy; heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference, flowing hot to cold.

concept_sections.heading: Specific heat
concept_sections.explanation: Warming (without phase change) needs $Q=mc\Delta T$. Water's high $c$ makes it slow to heat and cool.

concept_sections.heading: Phase changes
concept_sections.explanation: Melting and boiling absorb heat at constant temperature: $Q=mL$. Full heating curves combine $mc\Delta T$ and $mL$ segments.

concept_sections.heading: Thermal expansion
concept_sections.explanation: Materials generally expand when heated: $\Delta L=\alpha L\Delta T$ — the reason for expansion gaps in bridges and rails.

concept_sections.heading: Heat transfer
concept_sections.explanation: Heat moves three ways: conduction (contact), convection (fluid motion), and radiation (electromagnetic waves, no medium required).

real_world_examples.title: A metal spoon in soup
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Conduction carries heat along the metal, which conducts well.

real_world_examples.title: Boiling water for pasta
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Specific heat warms it to $100^\circ$C; latent heat drives the boiling.

real_world_examples.title: Feeling the sun's warmth
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Radiation transfers heat across empty space to your skin.
